summary: Summation No. 14 covers non-military Occupation activities in Japan for November 1946 (with economic statistics mostly for October and some for September). The dominant political event is the 3 November promulgation of the new Constitution, effective 3 May 1947; the report reproduces the Emperor's rescript, party and press reactions and a Government Section analysis. It then traces the Cabinet's six fundamental policies, the extension of the purge to local officials and business leaders, the electrical workers' dispute and Social Democrat demands for dissolution, and the opening of the 91st Extraordinary Diet. Part II adds crime, amnesty, judicial and war crimes material, including the Tokyo tribunal's tenth and eleventh phases. Part III supplies detailed production, transport, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property statistics, showing coal and power shortages, strikes and tentative export resumption. Part IV covers welfare, public health, education reform, religion and the media. Historians will find it useful for purge mechanics, constitutional commentary, labor politics and the state of the economy.
highlights: The new Constitution was promulgated on 3 November 1946 before the Emperor, Cabinet and Diet, to take effect on 3 May 1947; more than 100,000 people rallied at the Imperial Palace grounds.

On 4 November the Cabinet issued six fundamental policies, including popularizing the Constitution, educational reform, local self-government and a labor solution; Social Democrats attacked them and demanded resignation or Diet dissolution.

On 8 November the 4 January purge directive was extended to prefectural, city, town and village officials, later to business and publishing leaders; about 170,000 were estimated removed, postponing the December local elections.

On 6 November the Government rejected the Central Labor Relations Committee's compromise in the electrical workers' dispute, which had proposed a 500 yen minimum wage, fueling opposition demands for dissolution.
The Emperor's rescript of 3 November granted amnesty, commutation or restored civil rights to 331,400 persons, including 93,900 under general pardon.

Coal shortages and a 12-day strike cut Imperial Oil's October crude output to 12,496 kiloliters, the lowest of the Occupation; coal output was 1,766,800 metric tons and gas capacity was 77.6 percent idle.

At the Tokyo trials the prosecution finished its tenth phase (war preparations) on 4 November and began the eleventh (US-British-Japanese relations); 223 more suspects were ordered apprehended and 793 held in Sugamo.
Bank of Japan notes reached 74,816,000,000 yen on 30 November and national debt 227,639,000,000 yen on 31 October; 40 more companies controlling 860 subsidiaries were designated for liquidation.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover, title page, table of contents of the four parts, and list of 100 charts, maps and graphs for Summation No. 14 (November 1946).

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Monthly digest: no organizational change, Constitution promulgated 3 November, purge extended, electrical dispute, falling industrial output, 2,703,429 welfare recipients and education reform.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: One paragraph stating there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during November.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Constitution promulgated 3 November, the Cabinet's six policies of 4 November, purge extension, electrical dispute, party reactions, the 91st Diet and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of agriculture, mining, industry, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property; Bank of Japan notes reached 74.8 billion yen and 40 more companies were slated for liquidation.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Welfare spending of 144,192,802 yen, new Child Welfare Bureau, Ryukyuan repatriation, typhus, nine-year compulsory education recommendation, Shinto and funeral directives, and press comment on the Constitution.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics, public safety, and legal and war crimes affairs, centered on the Constitution, the purge extension to local officials and business, and Tokyo tribunal proceedings.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Constitution text and analysis, six Cabinet policies, purge extension to local officials and business, electrical dispute, party maneuvers, local government plans, Diet composition and the Emperor's Ibaraki tour.

sections.title: The Constitution
sections.summary: Emperor's rescript, Yoshida's radio address, MacArthur's eve-of-promulgation statement and party reactions; the Constitution takes effect 3 May 1947.

sections.title: Analysis of the Constitution
sections.summary: Press digest, then a Government Section comparative analysis of the Emperor, Diet, Cabinet, judiciary, bill of rights and war renunciation, with enforcement and conclusion.

sections.title: Government Policy
sections.summary: Text of the Cabinet's six fundamental policies of 4 November, with reaction of the parties and the press.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: On 8 November the 4 January directive was extended to local officials, with about 170,000 purgees estimated and elections postponed; later extended to business and publishing leaders.

sections.title: Labor and Politics
sections.summary: On 6 November the Government rejected the Central Labor Relations Committee's settlement in the electrical workers' dispute, prompting demands for dissolution.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Social Democrats under Tetsu Katayama attacked the Cabinet; the Democratic League revived; Communist and Government party positions.

sections.title: Local Government
sections.summary: Governors' conference with the Emperor, Home Minister's decentralization plan, postponed local elections, and proposed special city status for Osaka, Kyoto, Yokohama and Kobe.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: The 91st Extraordinary Diet convened 25 November for 30 days with five major bills; the Liberals held 148 seats.

sections.title: The Emperor and Structural Changes
sections.summary: Emperor toured Ibaraki Prefecture on 17-18 November amid press reports of rising popularity; a new council was created.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety and Intelligence
sections.summary: Orderly strikes, black-market raids with over 700 arrests, 173,776 offenses in September, new Metropolitan Police Juvenile Section, police reform proposal and amnesty of 331,400 persons.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: Legal reforms, Supreme Court independence, occupation court cases, war crimes work in Japan and the Philippines, and the Tokyo tribunal's tenth and eleventh phases.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and Japanese Judicial Administration
sections.summary: Lawyers' Law revision, bar convention of 10 November, Japanese courts divested of civil claims against United Nations nationals, amnesty rescript and Chief Justice Hosono's statement.

sections.title: War Crimes Investigation and Trials
sections.summary: Investigation of a massacre of 70 civilians in New Guinea; 223 persons ordered apprehended, 793 held in Sugamo, and 105 tried in Japan to date.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Philippine and Australian trial results; at Tokyo the tenth phase (war preparations) ended 4 November and the eleventh (US-British-Japanese relations) began, with testimony of Ballantine and Richardson.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Twelve sections on agriculture, industry, utilities, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property control, showing output held down by coal and power shortages.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Agrarian reform campaign with 630,000 posters and pamphlets, 1,002,000 tons of rice collected by 20 November, record sweet potato crop, October fish landings of 113,196 tons.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: October log output of 448,088,000 board feet, coal output of 1,766,800 tons, coal stockpiles down to 882,000 tons and a nine-point miners' incentive program.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke steady at 113,000 tons, falling steel output, 18,805 buildings constructed in October; shipbuilding, chemicals and machinery limited by coal and power.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Canning shifts to glass for lack of tin plate, pulp down 8 percent, record 231,729 syringes, 1,280 truck chassis, rubber output down 34.3 percent.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton yarn reached 20,830,000 pounds, 3,000,000 short of goal; raw silk, rayon and wool held back by seasonal labor loss and power curtailment.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 107,845 motor vehicles, 15,948,849 train kilometers, power generation of 2,493,417,000 kWh amid drought, Shinosumi hydro plant opened 16 October, gas capacity 77.6 percent idle.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: 946,283 telephones in service, facsimile telegraph authorized 14 November, new Tokyo-Sendai cable, and a Tokyo Shibaura strike cutting tube output.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Union membership of 4,122,209 in 14,697 unions, federation merger talks, first labor-industry meeting 10 November, electric power dispute mediation and theater strikes.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: First postwar shipment of 250,000 yards of silk fabric to the United States, export samples for China and Korea, and over 600,000 of 890,000 scheduled cotton bales arrived.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Government held 41 days of staple food on 31 October; rice collections well ahead of 1945, fish consumption down, charcoal and firewood prices raised, violations rising.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 74,816,000,000 yen, financial institutions split into new and old accounts, central insurance corporations ordered dissolved, national debt 227,639,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: SCAP Dollar Custody Account opened 4 November, six firms removed from restricted list, 40 more holding companies designated, 10 Zaibatsu families, plants held for reparations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education, religion, arts and media of expression, ending with a map of Japan.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Welfare aid to 2,703,429 persons, Child Welfare Bureau, Ryukyuan repatriation, penicillin price cut to 200 yen, narcotics registration, rising typhus and 190,727 births in October.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Educational Reform Committee's nine-year coeducation proposal, Shinto fund-raising ban, public funeral prohibition, Ise-Shima National Park on 20 November, and press, radio and film comment.

sections.title: Map of Japan
sections.summary: Closing page carrying the map of Japan.
